newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania evaluates crop losses after storms.
newsitem.headline: Romania evaluates crop losses after storms.

text.p: Heavy rain, hail and floods have damaged crops, including wheat and maize, on almost 100,000 hectares, the Agriculture Ministry said on Monday.
A ministry statement said adverse weather last week had damaged crops on 92,264 hectares in the southern counties of Teleorman and Olt and in Galati.
Twelve people drowned in western Romania on Sunday in flash floods and scores were injured by hail.
Of the 92,264 hectares, 35,046 ha were under wheat, 26,687 ha under maize, 7,575 under barley and 14,395 under sunflower, the ministry statement said.
The remaining 8,561 ha had been under other crops, including sugar beet and seasonal vegetables, it said.
It gave no equivalent in tonnes for the losses.
A source in the farming sector told Reuters the figures released by the ministry on Monday "represent only part of the damage" and he expected the losses to be more extensive.
Ministry officials were unavailable for comment.
Several local newspapers quoted Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu on Monday as saying losses amounted to some 100 billion lei.
Last week, Gavrilescu said Romania expected a bumper wheat crop of 7.07 million tonnes this year, compared to 3.1 million in 1996.
